analysis.investment_thesis: Bandhan Bank's microfinance roots give it access to an underserved market, but its promoter holding of only 39.74% — far below my 55% threshold — is a non-negotiable governance failure, and its concentrated MFI loan book makes it structurally vulnerable to rural credit stress cycles. Finance costs growing at 26.6% CAGR against revenue growth of only 7.8% CAGR signals spread compression, and ROE of 11.16% does not justify a 27.9x P/E.
key_strengths: Forward P/E of 10.92x suggests the market has already priced in significant bad news, offering optionality if asset quality recovers
Absolute profit levels have recovered strongly post-COVID (2,745 Cr in FY25 vs 126 Cr in FY22), showing the franchise is still intact
P/B of 1.14x is relatively modest for a bank with a differentiated distribution model in underpenetrated markets
key_risks: Microfinance/MFI loan book concentration creates lumpy, cyclical credit losses — this is not the steady, predictable earnings I require
Finance costs growing at 26.6% CAGR (5,157 to 10,458 Cr) while revenue grows at 7.8% CAGR — the spread math is deteriorating
OCF was deeply negative in FY23 (-4,245 Cr), underscoring the episodic and volatile nature of cash generation
red_flags: Promoter holding of 39.74% — significantly below my 55% minimum, the single most important qualitative test I apply
ROE of 11.16% is below my 15% threshold, meaning the bank is not earning adequate returns on capital at the current scale
Net profit of only 126 Cr in FY22 (vs 2,195 Cr in FY23) illustrates extreme earnings volatility — the opposite of what I seek
Finance costs surged from 5,157 Cr to 10,458 Cr in 3 years, growing more than 2x faster than revenues
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bandhan Bank was founded with a genuine mission to serve the unbanked, and that mission has commercial merit. But from a pure investment standpoint, the bank fails multiple criteria simultaneously. The promoter holding of 39.74% is the most fundamental concern — in my experience, promoters who hold less than 55% are less likely to act in minority shareholders' interests over the long run. Combined with the fact that this is essentially a microfinance-heavy bank where NPAs can spike violently (as seen in FY22), the business model lacks the durability I require.

The revenue and profit trajectory shows improvement (FY25 net profit of 2,745 Cr), and the forward P/E of 10.92x is arithmetically appealing. But I have learned not to be seduced by cheap-looking multiples in businesses with structural vulnerabilities. The MFI sector in India is under stress from over-leveraging at the borrower level, and Bandhan's balance sheet at 1.9 lakh Cr in total assets is built on a foundation that has proven fragile before. Until promoter holding stabilizes above 55% and ROE sustains above 15%, this does not meet my bar.
